requirements.description:
An array of comparator sets. If an {@link SemanticVersion} satisfies any of the comparator sets, it will be
considered part of this range. In other words, these comparator sets are ORed when evaluating inclusion.

title:
A `version range` is a set of `comparators` which specify versions that satisfy the range.

A `comparator` is composed of an operator (@link {SemanticVersionRange.Operation}) and a partial `version`
({@link SemanticVersion}) separated by optional whitespace. For example `>=1.0.0` or `>=1.0`.

Build metadata ({@link SemanticVersion#buildMetadata}) is syntactically permitted on the partial versions,
but is completely ignored, as it’s never relevant to whether any comparator matches a particular version.

The set of primitive operators is:
- `<` Less than
- `<=` Less than or equal to
- `>` Greater than
- `>=` Greater than or equal to
- `=` Equal.
If no operator is specified, then equality is assumed, so the equality operator is optional, but MAY be included.

For example, the comparator >=1.2.7 would match the versions `1.2.7`, `1.2.8`, and `2.5.3`, but not the versions `1.2.6` or `1.1.0`.
For a full description of how {@link SemanticVersion}s are ordered, see http://semver.org/.

Comparators can be joined by whitespace to form a comparator set, which is satisfied by the
intersection of all of the comparators it includes. For example, the comparator set `>=1.2.7 <=2.0.0` would match
the versions `1.2.8` and `2.0.0`, but not `2.0.1`.

In other words, whitespace can be thought of as an `&&` or `AND` operator.

A range is composed of one or more comparator sets, joined by `||`. A version matches a range if and only if every
comparator in at least one of the `||`-separated comparator sets is satisfied by the version. Comparator sets are
defined by the type {@link SemanticVersionRange.Requirement}.

For example, the range `>=1.2.7 <1.3.0` would match the versions `1.2.7`, `1.2.8`, and `1.2.99`, but
not the versions `1.2.6`, `1.3.0`, or `1.1.0`.

The range `1.2.7 || >=1.2.9 <2.0.0` would match the versions `1.2.7`, `1.2.9`, and `1.4.6`,
but not the versions `1.2.8` or `2.0.0`.

C3 always takes into consideration pre-release versions. This is done so that filtering, sorting, and labeling is
simpler. The primary motivation is highlighted by the following scenario:
- You are working on a new release, say `5.0.0`, but you have not fully finished or released it yet.
- During your QA cycle, you would like to test a release candidate for `5.0.0`, say `5.0.0-rc+1`.
- Specifying a range of `=5.0.0` should include `5.0.0-rc+1`.
In more exact terms, this means the following:
- `=5.0.0` -> `>=5.0.0-0 <=5.0.0`
- `>=5.0.0` -> `>=5.0.0-0 <=MAX`
- `>5.0.0` -> `>5.0.0 <=MAX`
- `<=5.0.0` -> `>=0.0.0 <=5.0.0`
- `<5.0.0` -> `>=0.0.0 <5.0.0-0`

The {@link SemanticVersionRange} type stores comparator sets in the {@link #requirements} field. Each entry in the
array represents a comparator set in the range. For example, `1.2.7 || >=1.2.9 <2.0.0` would be parsed into 2
{@link #requirements}, `>=1.2.7.0-0 <1.2.8-0` and `>=1.2.9-0 <2.0.0-0`.

Advanced operators include:
- `*` Wildcard
- `~` Tilde allows patch-level changes if a minor version is specified on the comparator. Allows minor-level changes if not.
- `^` Caret requirements allow parts that are right of the first nonzero part of the version to increase.
Allows changes that do not modify the left-most non-zero element in the [major, minor, patch] tuple.

Example ranges:
- `*` -> `>=MIN <=MAX`
- `8.*` -> `>=8.0.0-0 <9.0.0-0`
- `8.13.*` -> `>=8.13.0-0 <8.14.0-0`
- `~1.2.3` -> `>=1.2.3-0 <1.3.0-0`
- `~1.2` -> `>=1.2.0-0 <1.3.0-0` (Same as `1.2.*`)
- `~1` -> `>=1.0.0-0 <2.0.0-0` (Same as `1.*`)
- `~0.2.3` -> `>=0.2.3-0 <0.3.0-0`
- `~0.2` -> `>=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0-0` (Same as `0.2.*`)
- `~1.2.3-beta.2` -> `>=1.2.3-beta.2 <1.3.0-0`
- `^1.2.3` -> `>=1.2.3-0 <2.0.0-0`
- `^0.2.3` -> `>=0.2.3-0 <0.3.0-0`
- `^0.0.3` -> `>=0.0.3-0 <0.0.4-0`
- `^1.2.3-beta.2` -> `>=1.2.3-beta.2 <2.0.0-0`
Note that prereleases in the `1.2.3` version will be allowed, if they are greater than or equal to `beta.2`.
So, `1.2.3-beta.4` would be allowed, but `1.2.4-beta.2` would not, because it is a prerelease of a different [major, minor, patch].
- `^0.0.3-beta` -> `>=0.0.3-beta <0.0.4-0`
Note that prereleases in the `0.0.3` version only will be allowed, if they are greater than or equal to beta.
So, `0.0.3-pr.2` would be allowed.
